Step 12 exists, runs cleanly from a fresh R process in about 9 seconds (peak memory about 210 MB), and its outputs are in place: 13 CSV tables and 2 figures under /home/user/WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/04_output/12_qpcr/. The script is /home/user/WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/01_pipeline/12_qpcr.R (1127 lines, longest line 150 characters, ASCII only). I ran no git command that changes state; the orchestrating session's snapshot commit 9fc2f06 already holds exactly this script, the 13 tables and the 2 PNG files (the PDFs and session_info.txt differ only by time stamp after my last rerun).

What the step does. (1) Builds the per-animal table from the nine replicate-level files (40 animals, 720 wells, 149 non-detect wells) with explicit ID, group-size and Cq checks, and compares it with the hand-built consolidated file. (2) Repeats the legacy analysis on the consolidated file in both variants (non-detects dropped; set to config$qpcr$legacy_nondetect), aov plus TukeyHSD, and compares it with the knitted legacy output (parsed, not typed) and with the audit note. (3) Fits delta Cq ~ ploidy * treatment per gene three ways: complete cases; censored regression (survival::survreg, Gaussian, an animal with no detected well is right-censored at max_cycles minus its actin Cq); and the same with one-well animals as bounds. Each fit is run with all 32 animals and without failed samples, with fold changes, 95% intervals, Benjamini-Hochberg q across genes per term, leave-one-out p ranges, and, for simple effects in complete-case fits, Student and Welch tests on the two groups alone. (4) Reference gene: actin by group, group differences, failed samples by Tukey's outer fence, and every effect under three normalizations (delta Cq, raw Cq, raw Cq with actin Cq as covariate). (5) COX1 as a raw Cq with the tests the audit note lists. (6) Ten statement rows (nine sentences of the Discussion and Conclusions, quoted word for word) with numbers and rule-derived verdicts. (7) Two figures.

Main results. The consolidated file equals the mean of the detected wells in all 288 cells (9 genes x 32 animals); 44 cells are missing, all without a detected well. The legacy analysis is reproduced: 11 of 11 ANOVA tables and 88 of 88 TukeyHSD lines of the knitted output agree at the printed precision, and the 9 quoted F and p values of the audit note agree. Of the eight targets with replicate data, three are quantifiable by the MIQE 95% rule (HSC70, HATHaP2, HSP90), four are near the detection limit (DNMT1 16%, HAT 22%, MBD2 30%, HIF1A 31% non-detect wells of 64), and MeCP2 (77%) is not analysed. No term of any of the nine analysed genes passes the correction across genes (smallest q: heat 0.27, ploidy 0.49, interaction 0.54). HSP90, primary analysis (censored regression without the failed sample D_N_N05, actin Cq 35.26, outer fence 33.38): heat vs control 2.17-fold (95% CI 1.08 to 4.34, p = 0.030); triploid vs diploid 1.95-fold (0.98 to 3.91, p = 0.058); in control animals 2.10-fold (0.77 to 5.68), p = 0.139 in the two-way model and 0.031 (Welch) or 0.033 (Student) on the two control groups alone. The legacy ploidy p = 0.035 exists only when the failed sample's non-detect is set to Cq 45. Actin differs between ploidies by -1.68 cycles (p = 0.078) and, without the failed sample, between heat and control by 1.14 cycles (p = 0.12); within groups the target Cq follows the actin Cq with a slope below 1 for most genes (HSC70 0.68, 95% CI 0.56 to 0.80). The HSP90 heat effect is 2.17-fold as delta Cq, 1.90-fold (p = 0.077) with actin as covariate and 0.99-fold (p = 0.98) in raw Cq, while the ploidy effect keeps its direction (1.95, 2.21, 4.11-fold). COX1: group means within 0.29 cycles, heat minus control -0.19 cycles in diploids (p = 0.37) and +0.29 in triploids (p = 0.083), interaction p = 0.070, correlation with actin Cq 0.002, no nuclear reference. Verdicts: the six rows on mitochondrial abundance are not supported; the four rows on HSP90 are partly supported, with conditions.

What I could not do: nothing in the repository gives primer efficiencies, the COX1 template, or replicate-level data for SOD, ATP synthetase and COX1, so those limits stay. I did not edit README files, issues.md or run_config.R; proposed text is in the fields below.

caveats: Every delta Cq result is conditional on actin, the only reference gene, and the data argue against it as a stable reference (group differences of 1.1 to 1.7 cycles, within-group slopes below 1). The step reports this; it cannot repair it.

The primary analysis (censored regression without failed samples), the failed-sample rule (outer fence), the detection thresholds (95% and 50%) and the verdict rules (alpha 0.05, q 0.05, leave-one-out, normalization) are choices made in this step. All variants are in the tables, and the choices are settings at the top of the script, but the authors may choose differently.

An animal with one detected well of two is taken at that well in the main censored fit and as a bound in the second censored fit. The data cannot say which is right. For HAT, HIF1A and MBD2 (6 to 8 such animals each) the two fits differ, so these genes carry no firm estimate.

Margins are thin in two places: HSP90 is quantifiable with 61 of 64 wells detected (95.3%) in the all-animal set, and HAT sits exactly on the 50% threshold in diploid controls (8 of 16 wells). One more non-detect would change either class.

Two diploid heat animals with late actin (D_D_N11 at 30.02 and D_D_N16 at 31.47) lie above the inner fence but below the outer fence and stay in. D_D_N11 has unshifted targets and drives results: without it the HSP90 ploidy p is 0.007 and the heat p 0.052.

The small-sample correction of the censored regression is exact only when nothing is censored; with censoring it rests on my scratch simulation (4.5% to 6.0% rejection at 5%), which is not part of the repository.

Residuals of the complete-case fits depart from normality for DNMT1 (Shapiro p = 0.031), HATHaP2 (0.006), HIF1A (0.025), MBD2 (0.008) and SOD (0.010); the values are in qpcr_models.csv. No rank-based or robust alternative was added.
Simple effects are not adjusted for the four simple effects of a gene, and fold changes assume doubling per cycle; no primer efficiencies are in the repository.
SOD and ATP synthetase come from the consolidated file only: their detection class counts animals instead of wells, and one-well animals cannot be told from two-well animals.
The step reads one file from 08_archive (the knitted legacy output) and stops if it is absent. Other pipeline steps do not read the archive.

The quoted sentences are typed into the script from the Google Doc text of 2026-11-18. The step cannot detect later edits of the manuscript; locations are section, paragraph and sentence of that version.

Statement Q08 also names 5-mC changes, which belong to step 03 and are not evaluated here. The draft's phrase 'companion experiments' is not evaluated; by their IDs the qPCR animals are the same 32 animals as in the ELISA (an inference from the IDs).

The script is 1127 lines, four times the size of other steps, because I was told to keep step-specific functions inside it. The fitting and legacy-parsing functions could move to 02_R_functions later.
With include_acute_heat_shock = TRUE the acute animals are pooled into their treatment group; that path runs and was looked at once, but its results were not examined in detail.
PDF figures and session_info.txt carry a time stamp and show as modified in git after any rerun; CSV and PNG files do not.

result.issues_text:
### I-29 (S2) qPCR and "mitochondrial abundance" claims

Proposed status in the summary table: `needs decision; pipeline done (step 12)`.

**Update 2026-11-19 (step 12, `01_pipeline/12_qpcr.R`; tables in `04_output/12_qpcr/tables/`).** Every number below is regenerated by the step.
- *Inputs.* The hand-built consolidated file equals the mean of the detected wells of the replicate-level files in all 288 cells (9 genes x 32 animals). Its 44 missing cells are animals with no detected well (`qpcr_consolidated_check.csv`). SOD, ATP synthetase and COX1 exist only in the consolidated file.
- *Legacy analysis reproduced.* 11 of 11 ANOVA tables and 88 of 88 TukeyHSD lines of `08_archive/ELISA/dct_analysis_NA-to-45_COX1convert.md` agree at the printed precision; the nine F and p values quoted in the audit note agree (`qpcr_anova_legacy.csv`, `qpcr_tukey_legacy.csv`).
- *Mitochondrial abundance.* Group means of the raw COX1 Cq are 21.54, 21.36, 21.36 and 21.64 (diploid control, diploid heat, triploid control, triploid heat). Heat minus control is -0.19 cycles in diploids (p = 0.37) and +0.29 cycles in triploids (p = 0.083); interaction p = 0.070; smallest Tukey p = 0.38. The COX1 Cq does not follow the actin Cq (r = 0.002; the nine analysed targets: r = 0.53 to 0.93), which points to a separate template. No nuclear reference was measured on it, so no relative abundance can be formed (`qpcr_cox1.csv`). Six statement rows: not supported.
- *HSP90.* This replaces the earlier sentence that the clearer effect is induction by heat. Relative to actin, heat vs control is 2.17-fold (95% CI 1.08 to 4.34; p = 0.030; q = 0.27 across nine genes); within diploids p = 0.094, within triploids p = 0.146; interaction p = 0.84. Triploid vs diploid is 1.95-fold (0.98 to 3.91; p = 0.058; q = 0.49); in control animals 2.10-fold (0.77 to 5.68), p = 0.139 in the two-way model, p = 0.031 (Welch) and 0.033 (Student) in a test of the two control groups alone, Tukey p = 0.44. The legacy ploidy p = 0.035 arises only when the non-detect of the failed sample D_N_N05 is set to Cq 45. With one animal left out the heat p ranges from 0.015 to 0.055 and the ploidy p from 0.007 to 0.106. The heat effect depends on the normalization (new issue below); the ploidy difference keeps its direction under each normalization (`qpcr_models.csv`, `qpcr_normalization_check.csv`). Four statement rows: partly supported, with the conditions listed in `qpcr_manuscript_statements.csv`.
- *Several genes.* The legacy analysis normalized ten targets to actin and the draft names one. Across the nine genes that can be analysed no term has q < 0.05 (smallest q: heat 0.27, ploidy 0.49, interaction 0.54).
- *Design.* By their IDs the qPCR animals are the 32 animals of the ELISA (control 01 to 08 and heat 11 to 18 of each ploidy), so the qPCR, unlike the WGBS comparison (I-01), compares control and heat animals of one experiment. The draft calls them "companion experiments"; to be confirmed by the authors.
- The assessment in `07_documentation/audit/elisa_qpcr_audit.md`, section 3.3, needs the same correction.

**Options (extended).** (a) Remove the qPCR statements. (b) Keep HSP90 as an exploratory observation: describe the assay in Methods, report fold changes with intervals from `qpcr_models.csv`, and state that one unvalidated reference gene was used and that no effect survives correction across the genes measured. (c) For any statement about mitochondria, measure COX1 against a single-copy nuclear gene on the same DNA. Triploid nuclei hold 1.5 times the nuclear DNA, so a ratio to a nuclear gene needs that factor before ploidies are compared.

### I-xx (S2) Actin, the only reference gene, does not behave as a stable reference

**Evidence (step 12; `qpcr_reference_gene.csv`, `qpcr_normalization_check.csv`).** Actin Cq spans 21.9 to 35.3 across the 32 animals. It differs between ploidies by -1.68 cycles (95% CI -3.57 to 0.20; p = 0.078; -1.07 cycles, p = 0.14 without the failed sample) and, without the failed sample, between heat and control by 1.14 cycles (-0.32 to 2.60; p = 0.12). Within groups a target Cq rises by less than one cycle per cycle of actin: HSC70 0.68 (0.56 to 0.80), HATHaP2 0.59, SOD 0.54, HSP90 0.83 (0.57 to 1.10), ATP synthetase 0.88. Delta Cq therefore still depends on the amount of template, and animals with a late actin Cq read as high expressers. For HSP90, heat vs control is 2.17-fold as delta Cq, 1.90-fold (p = 0.077) with the actin Cq as covariate, and 0.99-fold (p = 0.98) in raw Cq. Under delta Cq seven of nine genes read as higher in heat animals.

**Why it matters.** Normalization to one reference gene needs evidence that the gene is stable under the conditions compared (Bustin et al. 2009, Clinical Chemistry 55:611, section 8.1). Every relative expression in the legacy analysis rests on actin.

**Needs.** Information from the authors (was a second reference gene run; RNA input and quality per sample) and a decision.

### I-xx (S2) Most qPCR targets were measured at or below their limit of detection

**Evidence (`qpcr_nondetects.csv`).** Non-detect wells among the 64 wells of the 32 animals: HSC70 0, HATHaP2 2, HSP90 3, DNMT1 10 (16%), HAT 14 (22%), MBD2 19 (30%), HIF1A 20 (31%), MeCP2 49 (77%). At the limit of detection 95% of wells are detected (Bustin et al. 2009, section 7.4.3), so of the eight targets with replicate-level data only HSC70, HATHaP2 and HSP90 are quantifiable. MeCP2 has no group with half its wells detected and is not analysed. ### I-29 (S2) qPCR and "mitochondrial abundance" claims

Proposed status in the summary table: `needs decision; pipeline done (step 12)`. Proposed change to the status of I-31: the qPCR part is done (step 12).

**Update 2026-11-19 (step 12, `01_pipeline/12_qpcr.R`; tables in `04_output/12_qpcr/tables/`).** Every number below is regenerated by the step. Statement IDs are those of `qpcr_manuscript_statements.csv` (11 rows).
- *Inputs.* For the nine genes that have a replicate-level file, the hand-built consolidated file equals the mean of the detected wells in all 288 cells (9 genes x 32 animals: 247 values compared, 41 missing in both). 41 of its 44 missing cells are animals with no detected well; the other 3 are in SOD (1) and ATP synthetase (2), which have no replicate-level file and cannot be checked (`qpcr_consolidated_check.csv`). SOD, ATP synthetase and COX1 exist only in the consolidated file.
- *Legacy analysis reproduced.* 11 of 11 ANOVA tables and 88 of 88 TukeyHSD lines of `08_archive/ELISA/dct_analysis_NA-to-45_COX1convert.md` agree at the printed precision; the nine F and p values quoted in the audit note agree (`qpcr_anova_legacy.csv`, `qpcr_tukey_legacy.csv`).
- *Mitochondrial abundance.* Group means of the raw COX1 Cq are 21.54, 21.36, 21.36 and 21.64 (diploid control, diploid heat, triploid control, triploid heat). Heat minus control is -0.19 cycles in diploids (p = 0.37) and +0.29 cycles in triploids (p = 0.083); interaction p = 0.070; smallest Tukey p = 0.38. The COX1 Cq does not follow the actin Cq (r = 0.002; the nine analysed targets: r = 0.53 to 0.93), which points to a separate template. No nuclear reference was measured on it, so no relative abundance can be formed (`qpcr_cox1.csv`). Seven statement rows (Q01 to Q05, Q09, Q11): not supported. Q05 is Discussion 4.5, paragraph 2, sentence 3 ("This finding is consistent with ..."), which only refers back to Q04 and goes with it.
- *HSP90, heat.* This replaces the earlier sentence that the clearer effect is induction by heat. Relative to actin, heat vs control is 2.17-fold (95% CI 1.08 to 4.34; p = 0.030; q = 0.27 across nine genes); within diploids p = 0.094, within triploids p = 0.146; interaction p = 0.84. With one animal left out p ranges from 0.015 to 0.055 and stays below 0.05 in 26 of 31 fits. The effect depends on the normalization (new issue below). Row Q07: partly supported, with four conditions.
- *HSP90, triploid vs diploid.* Averaged over treatments 1.95-fold (0.98 to 3.91; p = 0.058; q = 0.49). In control animals 2.10-fold (0.77 to 5.68), p = 0.139 in the two-way model, Tukey p = 0.44. A test of the two control groups alone gives p = 0.033 (Student) and 0.031 (Welch), but it depends on single animals: with one of the 15 control animals left out the Student p ranges from 0.003 to 0.073 and stays below 0.05 in 7 of 15 tests, the Welch p in 9 of 15. The legacy ploidy p = 0.035 arises only when the non-detect of the failed sample D_N_N05 is set to Cq 45 (0.068 when it is dropped). The direction holds under each normalization: in control animals 2.10-fold as delta Cq, 5.04-fold in raw Cq (p = 0.042), 2.42-fold with actin as covariate (p = 0.085) (`qpcr_models.csv`, `qpcr_normalization_check.csv`). Rows Q06, Q08, Q10: partly supported, with three conditions.
- *Several genes.* The legacy analysis normalized ten targets to actin and the draft names one. Across the nine genes that can be analysed no term has q < 0.05 (smallest q: heat 0.27, ploidy 0.49, interaction 0.54).
- *Design.* By their numbers the qPCR animals are the 32 animals of the ELISA (control 01 to 08 and heat 11 to 18 of each ploidy; compared by hand with `04_output/03_global_methylation/tables/elisa_percent_5mC.csv`, not by the step). If so, the qPCR, unlike the WGBS comparison (I-01), compares control and heat animals of one experiment. The draft calls them "companion experiments"; to be confirmed by the authors.
- The assessment in `07_documentation/audit/elisa_qpcr_audit.md`, section 3.3, needs the same correction.

**Options (extended).** (a) Remove the qPCR statements. (b) Keep HSP90 as an exploratory observation: describe the assay in Methods, report fold changes with intervals from `qpcr_models.csv`, and state that one unvalidated reference gene was used, that no effect survives correction across the genes measured, and that the difference between the control groups depends on single animals. (c) For any statement about mitochondria, measure COX1 against a single-copy nuclear gene on the same DNA. Triploid nuclei hold 1.5 times the nuclear DNA, so a ratio to a nuclear gene needs that factor before ploidies are compared. Not a replacement: the WGBS coverage files hold the mitochondrial genome (NC_001276.1), so a ratio of mitochondrial to nuclear coverage exists per library, but the control and heat libraries come from different cohorts and batches (I-01). This has not been computed.

### I-xx (S2) Actin, the only reference gene, does not behave as a stable reference

**Where.** Every relative expression of the legacy qPCR analysis; Discussion 4.5 and 4.7 (HSP90).

**Evidence (step 12; `qpcr_reference_gene.csv`, `qpcr_normalization_check.csv`).** Actin Cq spans 21.9 to 35.3 across the 32 animals. It differs between ploidies by -1.68 cycles (95% CI -3.57 to 0.20; p = 0.078; -1.07 cycles, p = 0.14 without the failed sample) and, without the failed sample, between heat and control by 1.14 cycles (-0.32 to 2.60; p = 0.12). Within groups a target Cq rises by less than one cycle per cycle of actin: HSC70 0.68 (0.56 to 0.80), HATHaP2 0.59, SOD 0.54, HSP90 0.83 (0.57 to 1.10), ATP synthetase 0.88. Delta Cq therefore still depends on the amount of template, and animals with a late actin Cq read as high expressers. For HSP90, heat vs control is 2.17-fold as delta Cq, 1.90-fold (p = 0.077) with the actin Cq as covariate, and 0.99-fold (p = 0.98) in raw Cq. Under delta Cq seven of nine genes read as higher in heat animals.

**Why it matters.** Normalization to one reference gene needs evidence that the gene is stable under the conditions compared (Bustin et al. 2009, Clinical Chemistry 55:611, section 8.1). Every relative expression in the legacy analysis rests on actin. The same pattern weakens the censored regression of step 12, whose censoring bound is 40 minus the actin Cq (header of the step).

**Needs.** Information from the authors (was a second reference gene run; RNA input and quality per sample) and a decision.

### I-xx (S2) Most qPCR targets were measured at or below their limit of detection

**Evidence (`qpcr_nondetects.csv`).** Non-detect wells among the 64 wells of the 32 animals: HSC70 0, HATHaP2 2, HSP90 3, DNMT1 10 (16%), HAT 14 (22%), MBD2 19 (30%), HIF1A 20 (31%), MeCP2 49 (77%). At the limit of detection 95% of wells are detected (Bustin et al. 2009, section 7.4.3), so of the eight targets with replicate-level data only HSC70, HATHaP2 and HSP90 are quantifiable. MeCP2 has no group with half its wells detected and is not analysed. For HAT, MBD2 and HIF1A six to eight animals have one detected well of two, and the result depends on how that well is read (MBD2 ploidy 0.91-fold or 1.53-fold; HIF1A interaction 0.52-fold or 1.06-fold; `qpcr_models.csv`).

**Proposed resolution.** Do not report DNMT1, MBD2, MeCP2, HIF1A or HAT as quantitative results.

### I-xx (S2) Substituting Cq 45 for non-detects creates values

**Evidence (`qpcr_sensitivity.csv`, `qpcr_reference_gene.csv`).** No detected Cq is later than 39.94, so the runs appear to have had 40 cycles, and no well can have a Cq of 45. With 45 substituted and actin subtracted, the failed sample D_N_N05 (actin Cq 35.26, above the outer fence of 33.38; 6 of its 8 targets have no detected well) becomes the highest "expression" of DNMT1 and HAT and the lowest of HSP90, which moves the legacy HSP90 ploidy p from 0.068 to 0.035. For MBD2 the heat effect has p = 0.009 with non-detects dropped, 0.67 with 45 substituted, and 0.090 in the censored regression. Both legacy treatments are biased (McCall et al. 2014, Bioinformatics 30:2310).

**Status.** pipeline done (step 12): both legacy variants are reproduced and a censored regression is reported beside them. The test of that regression was checked by simulation in the step: at a nominal 5% it rejects a true null in 4.5% to 5.95% of data sets, against 6.8% to 9.6% without the small-sample correction (`qpcr_censored_test_size.csv`).
